title: Canonical finite evaluation commutes with quotient transitions
statement: For a scheme morphism $g:X\to Y$ and an adic coefficient datum $d$, use the prescribed canonical finite interfaces of [def-cbc-completed-reduction-finite-interfaces], [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum], and [def-weil-pbc-completed-pullback]. For every completed-coefficient derived object $K$ and every $a\le b$ in $\mathbb N$ (representing positive exponents $a+1$ and $b+1$), the canonical finite evaluation at $b$ followed by restriction of the finite target quotient transition and the canonical composition of restriction equals the actual strict pulled tower transition from $b$ to $a$ followed by finite evaluation at $a$. This includes $a=b$, $a=0$, the zero complex, and arbitrary unbounded $K$. No completeness or quotient-flatness hypothesis is added.

source.place: Finite-reduction compatibility, the strict quotient-transition square used by adicPresentationFiniteIso_transition; Steps 4 and 7--8 of the former all-quotient coherence plan.

proof.text: The canonical ordinary finite comparisons commute with every quotient transition, including equal indices, by their normalized section formulas and the strict tower unit. Apply ordinary_finite_quotient_comparison.

On a K-flat cochain representative, use the existing normalizations of the finite evaluation comparison and finite target transition. Naturality of the universal tower counits identifies the pulled model transition. The exact restriction factorization is compatible with composition, so the ordinary quotient square gives equality after the finite model computation map. That map is invertible on K-flat representatives; cancel it.

The two composites are natural transformations out of the derived category. Every complex has a K-flat resolution, whose quasi-isomorphism becomes invertible. Naturality transports their equality on K-flat representatives to arbitrary complexes, and derived localization detects equality. Evaluate the resulting transformation equality at the arbitrary derived object K. No flatness of a quotient over the completed ring is assumed.

lean.statement:
theorem finite_quotient_transition_compatibility
    (K : DerivedCategory (pbcModules Y (pbcAdicCompletion Y d)))
    (a b : ℕ) (h : a ≤ b) :
    (completedReductionFiniteEvaluation g d b).hom.app K ≫
        (pbcDerivedRestrict (completedReductionProjection X d b)).map
          ((completedReductionTargetTransition g d a b h).app K) ≫
        (pbcDerivedRestrictComp (completedReductionProjection X d b)
          (reductionCoefficientMap X d b a h) (completedReductionProjection X d a)
          (completedReductionProjection_comp X d b a h)).hom.app
            ((completedReductionFiniteTarget g d a).obj K) =
      (pbcTowerTransition X (pbcAdicCompletion X d) b a h).app
          ((completedTowerPullback g d).obj ((completedReductionTower Y d).obj K)) ≫
        (completedReductionFiniteEvaluation g d a).hom.app K
